Each of the three recorded leaves was fetched and its H1 and breadcrumb confirmed: 'Bath Accessories + Organization' / 'Bathroom Faucets' / 'Bathroom Mirrors + Medicine Cabinets', all with breadcrumb Home > Bed + Bath > Bath. None of them has child collections, so the deepest-node rule is satisfied and the parent /collections/bath (83) is correctly NOT recorded. QTY: the collection grid is Algolia InstantSearch (app AVKHUU7E0V, search key 82a89b3b781da17c3ff1c020ea007984, index shopify_products), and the visible count is literally algolia.helpers.formatNumber(data.nbHits) - the instantSearchStatsTemplate in the page's own inline script renders `${algolia.helpers.formatNumber(data.nbHits)} ${algolia.translations.resultsFound}`, and the .ais-stats-container div is empty in the SSR HTML, i.e. that widget is the ONLY thing that ever prints a total on these pages. I replicated the query exactly as /cdn/shop/t/51/assets/algolia_instant_search.js builds it: filters = 'collections:""' (collection_id_indexing is true, so the handle - not the numeric id - is the facet value); NO stock filter (config.stock_policy == 'allow', so the stockPolicyFilter branch is skipped); ruleContexts = [, 'collection_page'] and analyticsTags the same (collection_id_query_rules is false, so collectionRulesContextValue is the handle); facetingAfterDistinct = false; and CRITICALLY the 'distinct' parameter is NOT sent at all, because the theme only sets it when instant.distinct is truthy and instant.distinct = !!algolia.config.show_products = false.
